label: input token v
explanation: Fires on every step where the input token is the letter v, in both the original and copy phases, and essentially nowhere else (dev P=1.00, R=0.998). The only extra activations are a few dozen weak ones on u/t/j/e/c. Magnitude depends on position. It is strongest when v is the last original token right before <DEL> (about 0.96-1.0 of max) and when v is at t=0 (about 0.93). It is moderate for v in the middle of the original phase (about 0.6-0.75) and weakest for v fed back during the copy phase (about 0.5-0.57). Original-phase activations carry about 61% of the mass. It never fires on <DEL> or on other tokens, and it does not depend on the output token or the previous token.

issues: The predicate and the label hold up. On the test split in_tok == tok('v') gets P=1.000, R=0.998, F1=0.999, mass recall 0.9996 and correlation 0.98. There are 0 false positives and 390 misses, which carry 0.0% of the activation mass.

The extra activations on non-v tokens follow a position pattern but have no mass. Adding (t==8)&(L==9) to the predicate cuts the test misses from 390 to 32, and those 32 are at step 7 at about 0.13. So the weak u/t/j/e/c hits sit almost entirely at the last original position of L=9 sequences (about 0.13-0.18 of max). This is a minor footnote, not a reason to change the predicate.

The magnitude claim is wrong. The explanation says v is strongest 'when v is the last original token right before <DEL> (about 0.96-1.0)'. In fact the 0.96-1.0 peak only happens at t=8, which only exists when L=9. When v is last before <DEL> in shorter sequences it is much weaker: L=4 (t=3) gives about 0.59-0.68, L=6 (t=5) about 0.65-0.75, L=8 (t=7) about 0.73-0.83. All top-activating examples are L=9, t=8.

The claim that v in the middle of the original phase is 'moderate (about 0.6-0.75)' is also off. In L=9 sequences, v at t=5-7 that is not the last token reaches 0.76-0.89 (examples: t=6 0.83, t=7 0.81, and 0.89 at t=6 in the test misses). Original-phase magnitude actually rises with absolute position t, with a separate high value at t=0 (about 0.93). It does not peak because v is adjacent to <DEL>.

These claims check out: no activation on <DEL>; copy-phase v is weakest (about 0.43-0.63); 61.4% of mass is in the original phase; no dependence on out_tok or prev_tok. The first_tok=v lift is just v at t=0.
